clean_body: | | | Peter, We just dropped a brand-new sticker inspired by the Working Families Guarantee — our pledge to working people in a time of skyrocketing costs, billionaire greed, and AI-driven job loss. And honestly, we think this belongs everywhere working people are (which is... everywhere). The Working Families Guarantee is about raising expectations for what all of us deserve — and this sticker helps carry that message everywhere it goes. Because this isn’t some impossible wishlist — it’s the bare minimum every person deserves. Things like: A good job. Affordable housing. Quality healthcare. Reliable childcare. That’s the floor , Peter. And right now, while billionaires rake in record profits and corporations try to replace workers with AI while driving up costs on the rest of us, more and more people are realizing the same thing: this economy is rigged against working families. But people are fighting back. Last week, WFP champions scored major primary wins in Pennsylvania by running on a simple idea: working people deserve leaders who will fight for them , not billionaires and corporations. And across the country, more and more voters are responding to that message. Now it’s time to bring that message everywhere we go. Slap the sticker on your water bottle, your laptop, your car bumper, your guitar case, your fridge (magnet required), or anywhere else people will see it and know: we’re done accepting crumbs while billionaires hoard the wealth working people create. body:
I want to tell you about some people who did something incredibly brave – and who need our help right now.
Peter,

I want to tell you about some people who did something incredibly brave—and who need our help right now.

When Donald Trump and Greg Abbott tried to push through a mid-decade gerrymander in Texas designed to push Black and Latino communities out of political power, Rep. Gene Wu and Texas House Democrats made a choice. They decided to stand up for their convictions and do what they thought was right.

So when the Supreme Court handed Republican legislatures a permission slip to rig maps, These Democrats used the last tool they had: they refused to be in the room. They refused to be complicit.

And they paid a real price for it.

They faced warrants for their arrest, lawsuits, bomb threats, financial penalties and efforts to expel them from the Legislature entirely.

Republicans want to make an example out of them. They want every Democratic lawmaker in this country to watch what happens to people who stand up for their principles and think twice before doing the same.

I've spent my career in Kentucky trying to show that when you lead with your principles and focus on helping people, you can win, even in tough places. And that our leaders must stand up for our convictions, even when it's hard. These Texas Democrats did exactly that. They put their careers, their safety, and their livelihoods on the line not for themselves, but for voters who were about to have their voices taken away.

So when the Supreme Court handed Republican legislatures a permission slip to rig maps, These Democrats used the last tool they had: they refused to be in the room. They refused to be complicit. name: Derek Tran
subject: Garden Grove Update: BLEVE Threat Eliminated. Here's what happened and how we responded:
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/dt-q2-2026?refcode=em-header [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/dt-q2-2026?refcode=em-header]
Friends,

I have important, and encouraging, news to share regarding the Garden Grove chemical crisis — which took place in the heart of my district in California.

The threat of a catastrophic explosion of the chemical tank at the center of this crisis has been eliminated. The Orange County Fire Authority and their partners worked through the night, and their heroic efforts paid off.

After five grueling days of uncertainty spent in shelters across Orange County, 50,000 evacuated residents were finally allowed to return home.

What happened:
A hazardous materials incident unfolded at GKN Aerospace — an aerospace facility in Garden Grove, CA. A tank holding approximately 6,000–7,000 gallons of a toxic, highly flammable chemical began leaking, with two additional tanks nearby containing more than 30,000 gallons of the same material.
Out of an abundance of caution, Orange County Fire Authority ordered the evacuation of roughly 50,000 residents. Evacuation sites were stood up and filled quickly around Orange County.
The situation was serious. Approximately 15% of residents initially declined to evacuate — something my office worked urgently to address.

What we did in response:
Immediately upon returning from Washington, D.C., I went directly to the incident command post to be briefed by local authorities and to make sure our community was supported.
Secured a Federal Emergency Declaration. At my urging, President Trump signed California's request for a Federal Emergency Declaration to support the ongoing response in Garden Grove. I worked around the clock to make sure our community had the federal resources needed to solve the immediate crisis and help displaced families return home. I'm grateful to Governor Newsom for his steadfast leadership, and to Senators Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff for working with me to make this happen.
Activated FEMA and EPA resources. I was in direct contact with FEMA to ensure they were fully briefed and on standby. The EPA dispatched a team on-site to monitor our air quality. With the federal declaration now signed, those resources are fully unlocked.
Visited evacuation site. I personally toured the evacuation centers to meet with displaced residents, listen to their concerns, and make sure they felt seen and supported — not just processed.
Held GKN Aerospace accountable. I called the company's president personally. I was direct: the displacement of 50,000 residents and the full cost of this emergency response is on them. I expect the company to take full ownership, and invited GKN Aerospace to attend my community meeting for residents impacted by the hazmat crisis.
Pushed hard to get people out. With 15% of residents still in the evacuation zone, blasted communications to students with families in the area and kept our phone lines open through this holiday weekend to help people in need. Every person and volunteer we could rally to help in the evacuation centers, we did.
Organized community phone banks. My team mobilized volunteers to call residents directly — checking in on vulnerable neighbors, sharing evacuation resources, and making sure no one was left without information. They also showed up to hand out meals and supplies to our displaced neighbors.

What comes next:
The immediate threat has passed, but our work is not finished. I have formally called for a deep investigation into what caused this incident — the inspection history, the engineering, and the oversight of that tank. The people of the 45th District deserve answers, and I will not stop pushing until we have them.

To the residents who had to leave their homes — your patience and your strength through this have been remarkable. To the first responders of the Orange County Fire Authority, Garden Grove PD, and every partner agency: you showed up when it mattered most, and this community owes you an enormous debt of gratitude.

To every local organization that opened its doors and every small business that donated food and supplies to help our neighbors — thank you.

And to every one of you reading this — thank you for staying engaged, informed, and showing up for each other. That is what makes this community worth fighting for.

Stay safe.

Derek Tran

Before you go:
Two organizations showed up for our community in a profound way during this crisis, and I want to make sure they're recognized. The American Red Cross of Southern California staffed our evacuation centers and made sure displaced families had a safe place to land. World Central Kitchen provided warm meals to those impacted by evacuations.
If you're looking for a way to turn your concern into action, consider supporting either organization — they were there for our neighbors when it counted most.

clean_body: Last week, I signed Paid Sick Leave into law in Virginia – because no one should have to choose between their health and their paycheck. | = | Hi Peter, Last week, I signed Paid Sick Leave into law in Virginia – because no one should have to choose between their health and their paycheck. = For over one million workers in this Commonwealth who currently have zero paid sick days, that changes everything. Here's what it means in practice: workers earn up to five paid days a year. Full-time and part-time workers alike are covered. Virginians who keep this economy running day to day now have a protection they've never had before. No one should have to show up sick because missing a shift means missing rent. That's not a standard that Virginians should accept. = | | | = | = | = | = | = Thank you, Governor Abigail Spanberger | | = Paid for by United for Virginia's Future PAC United for Virginia's Future PAC P.O. subject: Introducing: Your official Lt. Governor Democratic Nominee
disclaimer_text: paid for by the Vikki Goodwin Campaign, Allen Biehl, Treasurer**
body:
Now, I need your help to flip control of Texas' most powerful lawmaking body.
#
Friend,
**The Primary Runoff Election's results are in, and it's now official: I am your Democratic Nominee to defeat Dan Patrick this November.**
Now the hardest part of this race begins. Here’s the big picture:
[**We can only win in November if we're able to carry the momentum we've built so far into the General Election. Can I count on you to add your name to the team that's ready to defeat Dan Patrick?**](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22732?source=em20260527-1637&t=1&akid=1637%2E2118727%2EHWeCW2)
**[ADD YOUR NAME ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22732?source=em20260527-1637&t=2&akid=1637%2E2118727%2EHWeCW2)**
[__](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22732?source=em20260527-1637&t=3&akid=1637%2E2118727%2EHWeCW2)
_Friend, for over 10 years, Dan Patrick controlled Texas' most powerful lawmaking body to further his MAGA extremist agenda_ (Mid-term redistricting? Sharia Law? Ten Commandments?) _and hurt working families._
_**While billionaires and corporate insiders get special treatment, Texans are told to settle for less.**_
Together, we can change that.
I have spent years in the Texas Legislature fighting for public education, protecting clean water, expanding access to health care, and standing up for working families—not wealthy donors looking to cash in on Texas politics.
Now, I am ready to be a Lieutenant Governor that actually listens to Texans and solves real problems.
**[Friend, this is the year Democrats can win in Texas. Dan Patrick's far-right agenda makes him vulnerable. Will you be a part of our team to defeat him this November by signing your name today?](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22732?source=em20260527-1637&t=4&akid=1637%2E2118727%2EHWeCW2)**
**[JOIN THE TEAM ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22732?source=em20260527-1637&t=5&akid=1637%2E2118727%2EHWeCW2)**
Let's win this,
Rep. Vikki Goodwin

|

I’m reaching out because she’s working her tail off (get it) on her campaign, and her birthday is TODAY 🎂 And since I cannot legally buy her a present — something about “being a dog” and “not having any money” — I thought maybe we could surprise her another way. Frankly? All this running around even makes _me_ tired! So for her birthday, I’d love to help give her campaign a little extra _paw-mentum_ 🐾

I’m overwhelmed with gratitude.
Because of this grassroots team, I am officially the Democratic nominee for Congress in Georgia's 13th District.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?]

This campaign has always been about something bigger than one person. It’s about fighting for a country where science matters, where democracy is protected, and where working families have leaders who will actually work for them.
And now, we move forward together into the general election.
I don’t take this responsibility lightly. I know the months ahead will not be easy. National Republicans are already targeting races across Georgia because they know control of the House — and the direction of our state — could come down to seats like this one.
They have corporations and extremist allies behind them. But we have something stronger: people.
People who are tired of attacks on public education and public health. People who believe politicians shouldn’t be rigging maps or silencing voters to stay in power. People who want leaders grounded in facts, compassion, and integrity.
That’s the coalition we’re building together. As we head into November, I’m asking if you can make a donation to help us start the next phase of this campaign off strong. Chip in here >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?]
I’m so proud of what we’ve built already, and even more hopeful about what we can accomplish together.
Thank you for believing in this campaign. Thank you for believing in me.
Now let’s go win this thing.

_**by Dana DuBois**_
Dr. Oz and the Trump administration would like us all to know America is "under-babied."
And they're (uncharacteristically) not wrong. Birth rates are down, with a total fertility rate of 1.6 children per woman, the lowest ever recorded, according to the Population Reference Bureau. Low birth rates threaten our long-term economic viability, as we lack able-bodied young people to replace our aging population.
So yes, it's in the nation's interest to maintain a healthy birth rate.
And yet, here we are. Teen pregnancy rates are down, and Republicans think it's a bad thing. Young adults are delaying marriage and parenthood. And rather than asking why Americans might feel hesitant about bringing children into this particular moment in history, the pronatalist MAGA right has decided the problem is cultural decadence, feminism, career women, and ladies with too many cats.
Women need to log off Slack, put on prairie dresses, go full tradwife and start making babies again, I guess.
Except many young Americans are having the exact opposite reaction. And can you blame them? If you wanted to design a society specifically engineered to make people feel terrified of parenthood, you would probably build something pretty close to modern America.
A country increasingly incapable of nurturing the people already here.
I'm a GenX mom with two teen daughters. One of them is queer. I've spent years parenting through political whiplash, climate anxiety, the death of Roe v. Wade, economic instability, school shooting drills, healthcare fears, skyrocketing inflation, anti-trans legislation, online radicalization, and now the looming possibility AI may wipe out huge sectors of professional work before my high schoolers even graduate college.
I'm watching the Epstein files unfold in real time, atrocity after atrocity surfacing without consequence for the billionaire-class men involved.
I'm reading in horror about websites like Motherless hosting 20,000+ "sleep porn" videos of unconscious women being raped by their partners, while the news cycle barely blips.
So when I hear the official diagnosis is that younger people just need to chill out and make more babies?
Dr. Oz, my dude. That's _so_ not going to happen.
And it's not because young people are too lazy, shallow, or liberal.
It's because Americans--and especially women--no longer trust the country their children would inherit.

## **Don 't believe me? I've got eight reasons that might convince you.**
### 1\. Women No Longer Need to Marry for Survival
For much of human history, marriage was motivated by economics. Women needed men because women were systematically denied access to money, credit, careers, property ownership, and independent stability. We only gained the right to our own mortgages and credit cards in 1974, and to business credit in 1988. That's the year I graduated high school. This is not ancient history. All of this has happened within my lifespan.
What happened once we gave women access to credit?
Women now graduate college at higher rates than men. They build careers. They support themselves financially. They pay their own bills. Which means heterosexual relationships increasingly require something deeper than "find a guy with a paycheck."
Meanwhile, large numbers of GenZ men are being radicalized online into grievance politics and manosphere resentment. Women are being told they should submit more, tolerate more, shrink more, and need less.
Many respond with a single coherent thought: _No, thanks_.
That's not proof of societal collapse. It's evidence women finally have the autonomy to reject bad deals.
### 2\. Pregnancy Has Become More Dangerous in America
America already had one of the highest maternal mortality rates in the developed world before Roe v. Wade fell.
Now it's even riskier.
Restricting abortion access doesn't only impact women who need abortions. The ripple effect is catastrophic across the full spectrum of reproductive health, and especially on pregnant women.
Women are now being denied miscarriage care. Doctors delay emergency treatment because hospital legal teams need to determine whether saving a woman's life might violate abortion bans. OB-GYNs leave restrictive states entirely. Rural maternity wards are disappearing.
Women have been delayed or turned away at emergency rooms with potentially fatal conditions like ectopic pregnancies.
Nevaeh Crain. Josseli Barnica. Yeniifer Alvarez-Estrada Glick.
Women are dying.
And even outside catastrophic pregnancy scenarios, healthcare itself feels increasingly unstable. Millions of Americans are one layoff away from losing insurance coverage. ACA premiums have increased ~30%, with approximately 1.2 million families dropping their benefits due to costs. Younger adults are staring at a healthcare system where remaining insured feels financially precarious at best.
Pregnancy is always an act of vulnerability. But America has transformed it into an act of medical roulette.
Can we blame prospective parents for taking a pass?
* * *
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.WlmBAjjBeFbFNybPhGaCyuYyAwTUiREUHvLt9hdBWxI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=199156206)
* * *
### 3\. We're All Watching the Government Target LGBTQ+ Kids
Nearly 30% of GenZ adults identify as LGBTQ -- and 2.8% identify as transgender.
Threats toward marriage equality and trans safety aren't abstract for younger generations. Even people who aren't queer themselves know the odds are good that someone they love--a friend, sibling, partner, or future child--might be.
And now we're watching politicians escalate rhetoric around trans people from disagreement into something far darker.
The White House recently rolled out a so-called U.S. Counterterrorism Strategy referencing "radical transgender ideology" as part of broader extremism concerns. The document concludes with the line: _" We will find you and we will kill you."_
The administration would argue that line refers to terrorists broadly. But when you place "radical transgender ideology" inside a counterterrorism framework and then end with language like that, parents of queer and trans kids aren't irrational for hearing a threat.
My own daughter spent a few months identifying as trans when she was 11 years old. To call her a terrorist is laughably absurd.
But I'm not laughing.
To imagine her, or any child, folded into rhetoric about extremism and terrorism is grotesque.
And to imagine your own future child growing up inside that political climate?
That kind of rhetoric doesn't make people want to build families. It makes them terrified of what their families would inherit.
### 4\. The Future Looks Increasingly Dystopian and Uninhabitable
This week brought a headline warning that we should start evacuating New Orleans now, as it's reached the "point of no return" due to rising sea levels and will be underwater within decades. It barely made a splash in the news.
Meanwhile, wildfires scorch entire towns. Water shortages reshape the American West. Insurance companies are fleeing climate-vulnerable states because the math no longer works. Summers keep getting hotter. Storms keep getting stronger.
Scientists keep warning we're running out of time to meaningfully slow this down. It's dire, it's deadly, and it's dystopian AF.
Are young adults supposed to ignore this urgent situation and just carry on? What would be the psychologically healthy response to watching governments knowingly fail to protect the literal habitability of the planet?
I won't likely live to fully witness the devastation.
But my kids will.
If I'd known how untenable the climate change crisis would become so quickly, I might've made different choices.

* * *
### 5\. AI Is Making the Future of Work Unknowable
Even people with stable careers increasingly feel one corporate RIF away from professional extinction.
I work in tech. Every day I quietly wonder whether I have another year left before some executive decides AI can do enough of my job badly enough that replacing humans no longer matters.
But I say that as someone with savings, home equity, and decades of work history behind me.
Imagine being 27.
Imagine trying to commit to eighteen years of raising a child while the CEO of Microsoft AI casually predicts that all white-collar work will be automatable by AI in the next 18 months. The social contract underneath adulthood is collapsing in real time.
People aren't hesitating because they're selfish. They're hesitating because the ground beneath them no longer feels stable.
### 6\. Childcare, Healthcare, and College Have Become Financially Absurd
If America wanted more babies, it could start by supporting the families already here.
The United States remains the only OECD country without a national paid parental leave policy. More than 35% of U.S. counties are maternity care deserts, affecting more than 2.3 million women of reproductive age. For those lucky enough to have employer-sponsored family health insurance, out-of-pocket costs went up 6% in 2025 and now average nearly $7,000 a year.
And childcare? For many families, it's a second housing payment. This was true with my children back in 2012, and costs have gone up 40% in the past decade.
And then there's college.
Public university tuition has increased more than 175% over the past two decades, dramatically outpacing wage growth and inflation. Millennials and GenZ came of age watching older siblings and peers emerge from college carrying tens or even hundreds of thousands of dollars in student debt, into an economy that no longer guarantees stability in return.
Previous generations largely viewed college as a pathway into the middle class. Younger Americans increasingly view it as a financial gamble--with the odds stacked for the house, not them.
This means many prospective parents aren't just calculating the cost of diapers and daycare. They're staring down the future cost of educating a child in a system that feels punitive at nearly every stage of life.
The United States simply isn't a pro-family country. It's a country that talks endlessly about family while making family life logistically, medically, and financially brutal.
Paid leave. Affordable childcare. Public education. Maternal healthcare. Elder care. Community infrastructure. School safety. These aren't luxuries. They're the conditions under which families can function.
Instead, caregiving labor is treated as invisible work, largely dumped onto women until they disappear beneath the weight of it. We claim to worship family while structurally abandoning caregivers at every level.
It's difficult to take America's family rhetoric seriously when the people doing the caregiving are drowning, and the expenses are staggering.
* * *
[Leave a comment](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=199156206&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk5MTU2MjA2LCJpYXQiOjE3Nzk5MDYxOTcsImV4cCI6MTc4MjQ5ODE5NywiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.-LninoWkguudL3pe-MjBN0vA_UPs0eFqB3Mjx8pHhK4&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment)
* * *
### 7\. Parenting Has Become Isolating and Unsupported
Modern parenting increasingly happens without villages, extended family support, neighborhood connection, affordable housing near relatives, or trusted institutions. Many parents are raising children while simultaneously caring for aging parents, working full-time, and trying to survive economically in cities where community itself has become fragmented and transient.
Previous generations often had built-in support systems, even imperfect ones. Today, many families are privately white-knuckling modern life behind closed doors, wondering why everything feels so impossibly hard.
You cannot keep stripping communities for parts and then act surprised when people hesitate to create more vulnerable humans inside them.
### 8\. The People Demanding More Babies Seem to Deeply Dislike Women
Possibly the strangest part of the pronatalist panic is how many of the loudest voices demanding more babies also seem openly contemptuous of the people expected to produce them.
The rhetoric isn't subtle. It's overt vitriol.
Megachurch pastor Mark Driscoll referred to women as "penis homes," reducing women to vessels for male desire and reproduction. Nick Fuentes declared, "Your body, my choice," called women "the number one political enemy in America," and joked--_was it even a joke?_ --about "breeding gulags" for women. Republican lawmakers openly debate rolling back no-fault divorce while simultaneously stripping abortion rights and restricting reproductive healthcare. Even our voting rights are up for public debate.
Women are paying attention.
The message underneath it all feels unmistakable: your body belongs first to the state, the church, the nation, the husband, the baby -- and only distantly to you.
The modern MAGA pronatalist movement keeps demanding more babies while simultaneously trying to make women less safe, less autonomous, and more economically dependent. Then it acts outraged when women withdraw.
Some women hear their hatred and feel outright terror. Others may not consciously frame it that way, but respond instinctively by delaying motherhood, rejecting marriage, or opting out entirely.
This is an entirely rational response.
Because if your version of "pro-family" begins with stripping women of rights, mocking our independence, and reducing us to reproductive infrastructure, then a lot of women are going to hear that message and think:
_**Abso-fucking-lutely not**_.
* * *
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.WlmBAjjBeFbFNybPhGaCyuYyAwTUiREUHvLt9hdBWxI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=199156206)
* * *
So maybe America isn't "under-babied."
Maybe Americans are under-supported.
Maybe younger women aren't rejecting motherhood because they're selfish, shallow, decadent, or too attached to their careers or cats.
Maybe they're responding rationally to a country that increasingly feels unstable, unaffordable, hostile to vulnerability, and openly contemptuous of the people expected to hold families together.
Because if women are being told to have more babies while simultaneously losing rights, losing autonomy, losing economic security, losing healthcare access, and listening to powerful men openly describe us as breeding infrastructure?
Of course many of us are recoiling.
Many women stopped interpreting all of this as isolated hypocrisy and started recognizing something deeper: _**the United States hates women**_.
Or at a minimum, it's profoundly indifferent to our suffering.
The solution isn't demanding more babies from overwhelmed, world-wary woman.
The solution is building a country where raising one feels safe, sustainable, and possible. But that requires becoming a country capable of caring about women in the first place.
Right now: we are motherless.
And until that changes, I wouldn't expect America's "under-babied" problem to improve anytime soon.

Dr. Oz wants us to make more babies. But a country that refuses to protect women shouldn't be surprised when women hesitate to raise children inside it. | | and | May 27 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- by Dana DuBois Dr. Oz and the Trump administration would like us all to know America is "under-babied." And they're (uncharacteristically) not wrong. Birth rates are down, with a total fertility rate of 1.6 children per woman, the lowest ever recorded, according to the Population Reference Bureau. Low birth rates threaten our long-term economic viability, as we lack able-bodied young people to replace our aging population. So yes, it's in the nation's interest to maintain a healthy birth rate. And yet, here we are. Teen pregnancy rates are down, and Republicans think it's a bad thing. Young adults are delaying marriage and parenthood. And rather than asking why Americans might feel hesitant about bringing children into this particular moment in history, the pronatalist MAGA right has decided the problem is cultural decadence, feminism, career women, and ladies with too many cats. Women need to log off Slack, put on prairie dresses, go full tradwife and start making babies again, I guess. Except many young Americans are having the exact opposite reaction. And can you blame them? If you wanted to design a society specifically engineered to make people feel terrified of parenthood, you would probably build something pretty close to modern America. A country increasingly incapable of nurturing the people already here. I'm a GenX mom with two teen daughters. One of them is queer. I've spent years parenting through political whiplash, climate anxiety, the death of Roe v. Wade, economic instability, school shooting drills, healthcare fears, skyrocketing inflation, anti-trans legislation, online radicalization, and now the looming possibility AI may wipe out huge sectors of professional work before my high schoolers even graduate college. I'm watching the Epstein files unfold in real time, atrocity after atrocity surfacing without consequence for the billionaire-class men involved. I'm reading in horror about websites like Motherless hosting 20,000+ "sleep porn" videos of unconscious women being raped by their partners, while the news cycle barely blips. So when I hear the official diagnosis is that younger people just need to chill out and make more babies? Dr. Oz, my dude. That's so not going to happen. And it's not because young people are too lazy, shallow, or liberal. It's because Americans--and especially women--no longer trust the country their children would inherit. Blue Amp Media is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. Don 't believe me? I've got eight reasons that might convince you. 1\. Women No Longer Need to Marry for Survival For much of human history, marriage was motivated by economics. Women needed men because women were systematically denied access to money, credit, careers, property ownership, and independent stability. We only gained the right to our own mortgages and credit cards in 1974, and to business credit in 1988. That's the year I graduated high school. This is not ancient history. All of this has happened within my lifespan. What happened once we gave women access to credit? Women now graduate college at higher rates than men. They build careers. They support themselves financially. They pay their own bills. Which means heterosexual relationships increasingly require something deeper than "find a guy with a paycheck." Meanwhile, large numbers of GenZ men are being radicalized online into grievance politics and manosphere resentment. Women are being told they should submit more, tolerate more, shrink more, and need less. Many respond with a single coherent thought: No, thanks. That's not proof of societal collapse. It's evidence women finally have the autonomy to reject bad deals. 2\. Pregnancy Has Become More Dangerous in America America already had one of the highest maternal mortality rates in the developed world before Roe v. Wade fell. Now it's even riskier. Restricting abortion access doesn't only impact women who need abortions. The ripple effect is catastrophic across the full spectrum of reproductive health, and especially on pregnant women. Women are now being denied miscarriage care. Doctors delay emergency treatment because hospital legal teams need to determine whether saving a woman's life might violate abortion bans. OB-GYNs leave restrictive states entirely. Rural maternity wards are disappearing. Women have been delayed or turned away at emergency rooms with potentially fatal conditions like ectopic pregnancies. Nevaeh Crain. Josseli Barnica. Yeniifer Alvarez-Estrada Glick. Women are dying. And even outside catastrophic pregnancy scenarios, healthcare itself feels increasingly unstable. Millions of Americans are one layoff away from losing insurance coverage. ACA premiums have increased ~30%, with approximately 1.2 million families dropping their benefits due to costs. Younger adults are staring at a healthcare system where remaining insured feels financially precarious at best. Pregnancy is always an act of vulnerability. But America has transformed it into an act of medical roulette. Can we blame prospective parents for taking a pass? 3\. We're All Watching the Government Target LGBTQ+ Kids Nearly 30% of GenZ adults identify as LGBTQ -- and 2.8% identify as transgender. Threats toward marriage equality and trans safety aren't abstract for younger generations. Even people who aren't queer themselves know the odds are good that someone they love--a friend, sibling, partner, or future child--might be. And now we're watching politicians escalate rhetoric around trans people from disagreement into something far darker. The White House recently rolled out a so-called U.S. Counterterrorism Strategy referencing "radical transgender ideology" as part of broader extremism concerns. The document concludes with the line: " We will find you and we will kill you." The administration would argue that line refers to terrorists broadly. But when you place "radical transgender ideology" inside a counterterrorism framework and then end with language like that, parents of queer and trans kids aren't irrational for hearing a threat. My own daughter spent a few months identifying as trans when she was 11 years old. To call her a terrorist is laughably absurd. But I'm not laughing. To imagine her, or any child, folded into rhetoric about extremism and terrorism is grotesque. And to imagine your own future child growing up inside that political climate? That kind of rhetoric doesn't make people want to build families. It makes them terrified of what their families would inherit. 4\. The Future Looks Increasingly Dystopian and Uninhabitable This week brought a headline warning that we should start evacuating New Orleans now, as it's reached the "point of no return" due to rising sea levels and will be underwater within decades. It barely made a splash in the news. Meanwhile, wildfires scorch entire towns. Water shortages reshape the American West. Insurance companies are fleeing climate-vulnerable states because the math no longer works. Summers keep getting hotter. Storms keep getting stronger. Scientists keep warning we're running out of time to meaningfully slow this down. It's dire, it's deadly, and it's dystopian AF. Are young adults supposed to ignore this urgent situation and just carry on? What would be the psychologically healthy response to watching governments knowingly fail to protect the literal habitability of the planet? I won't likely live to fully witness the devastation. But my kids will. If I'd known how untenable the climate change crisis would become so quickly, I might've made different choices. 5\. AI Is Making the Future of Work Unknowable Even people with stable careers increasingly feel one corporate RIF away from professional extinction. I work in tech. Every day I quietly wonder whether I have another year left before some executive decides AI can do enough of my job badly enough that replacing humans no longer matters. But I say that as someone with savings, home equity, and decades of work history behind me. Imagine being 27. Imagine trying to commit to eighteen years of raising a child while the CEO of Microsoft AI casually predicts that all white-collar work will be automatable by AI in the next 18 months. The social contract underneath adulthood is collapsing in real time. People aren't hesitating because they're selfish. They're hesitating because the ground beneath them no longer feels stable. 6\. Childcare, Healthcare, and College Have Become Financially Absurd If America wanted more babies, it could start by supporting the families already here. The United States remains the only OECD country without a national paid parental leave policy. More than 35% of U.S. counties are maternity care deserts, affecting more than 2.3 million women of reproductive age. For those lucky enough to have employer-sponsored family health insurance, out-of-pocket costs went up 6% in 2025 and now average nearly $7,000 a year. And childcare? For many families, it's a second housing payment. This was true with my children back in 2012, and costs have gone up 40% in the past decade. And then there's college. Public university tuition has increased more than 175% over the past two decades, dramatically outpacing wage growth and inflation. Millennials and GenZ came of age watching older siblings and peers emerge from college carrying tens or even hundreds of thousands of dollars in student debt, into an economy that no longer guarantees stability in return. Previous generations largely viewed college as a pathway into the middle class. Younger Americans increasingly view it as a financial gamble--with the odds stacked for the house, not them. This means many prospective parents aren't just calculating the cost of diapers and daycare. They're staring down the future cost of educating a child in a system that feels punitive at nearly every stage of life. The United States simply isn't a pro-family country. It's a country that talks endlessly about family while making family life logistically, medically, and financially brutal. Paid leave. Affordable childcare. Public education. Maternal healthcare. Elder care. Community infrastructure. School safety. These aren't luxuries. They're the conditions under which families can function. Instead, caregiving labor is treated as invisible work, largely dumped onto women until they disappear beneath the weight of it. We claim to worship family while structurally abandoning caregivers at every level. It's difficult to take America's family rhetoric seriously when the people doing the caregiving are drowning, and the expenses are staggering. 7\. Parenting Has Become Isolating and Unsupported Modern parenting increasingly happens without villages, extended family support, neighborhood connection, affordable housing near relatives, or trusted institutions. Many parents are raising children while simultaneously caring for aging parents, working full-time, and trying to survive economically in cities where community itself has become fragmented and transient. Previous generations often had built-in support systems, even imperfect ones. Today, many families are privately white-knuckling modern life behind closed doors, wondering why everything feels so impossibly hard. You cannot keep stripping communities for parts and then act surprised when people hesitate to create more vulnerable humans inside them. 8\. The People Demanding More Babies Seem to Deeply Dislike Women Possibly the strangest part of the pronatalist panic is how many of the loudest voices demanding more babies also seem openly contemptuous of the people expected to produce them. The rhetoric isn't subtle. It's overt vitriol. Megachurch pastor Mark Driscoll referred to women as "penis homes," reducing women to vessels for male desire and reproduction. Nick Fuentes declared, "Your body, my choice," called women "the number one political enemy in America," and joked--was it even a joke? --about "breeding gulags" for women. Republican lawmakers openly debate rolling back no-fault divorce while simultaneously stripping abortion rights and restricting reproductive healthcare. Even our voting rights are up for public debate. Women are paying attention. The message underneath it all feels unmistakable: your body belongs first to the state, the church, the nation, the husband, the baby -- and only distantly to you. The modern MAGA pronatalist movement keeps demanding more babies while simultaneously trying to make women less safe, less autonomous, and more economically dependent. Then it acts outraged when women withdraw. Some women hear their hatred and feel outright terror. Others may not consciously frame it that way, but respond instinctively by delaying motherhood, rejecting marriage, or opting out entirely. This is an entirely rational response. Because if your version of "pro-family" begins with stripping women of rights, mocking our independence, and reducing us to reproductive infrastructure, then a lot of women are going to hear that message and think: Abso-fucking-lutely not. So maybe America isn't "under-babied." Maybe Americans are under-supported. Maybe younger women aren't rejecting motherhood because they're selfish, shallow, decadent, or too attached to their careers or cats. Maybe they're responding rationally to a country that increasingly feels unstable, unaffordable, hostile to vulnerability, and openly contemptuous of the people expected to hold families together. Because if women are being told to have more babies while simultaneously losing rights, losing autonomy, losing economic security, losing healthcare access, and listening to powerful men openly describe us as breeding infrastructure? Of course many of us are recoiling. Many women stopped interpreting all of this as isolated hypocrisy and started recognizing something deeper: the United States hates women. Or at a minimum, it's profoundly indifferent to our suffering. The solution isn't demanding more babies from overwhelmed, world-wary woman. The solution is building a country where raising one feels safe, sustainable, and possible. But that requires becoming a country capable of caring about women in the first place. Right now: we are motherless. And until that changes, I wouldn't expect America's "under-babied" problem to improve anytime soon. Blue Amp Media is a reader-supported publication. Hey Patriot,

clean_body: I cannot imagine a better place in the country to enjoy, explore, and protect the planet than Northwest Washington. | | | | I am proud to be endorsed by the Sierra Club Washington StateChapter. Sierra Club's slogan is "Enjoy, explore, and protect the planet." I cannot imagine a better place in the country to do just that than Northwest Washington. Our district is one of the most scenic and diverse in the country. Northwest Washington's natural resources are some of the prides of our nation. We represent the Puget Sound, America's largest estuary, as well as vital species like our orcas and salmon that call those waters home. From rolling hills, stunning valleys, and beautiful landscapes along the Puget Sound and the Salish Sea to our diverse ecosystem that supports large migrations of shore birds, beloved salmon returns, and the iconic bald eagle. Northwest Washington is beloved by environmentalists and adventurers alike. Washington is a beautiful state, and it is a privilege to work with the Sierra Club's Washington chapter to mitigate climate change and protect our home. body:
Our winning streak continued in Texas last night — two fearless fighters are headed to the halls of power to fight for working people.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260527-1&t=1&akid=3528%2E587540%2EgHoHED)
Peter,
**Last night, Leaders We Deserve-endorsed candidates Christian Menefee and Julio Salinas won their elections in Texas. Congrats, Christian and Julio! 🎉**
Voters in HD-41 knew exactly what was at stake in Julio’s race. They looked at their options — a wealthy, establishment-backed Democrat who is part of the same broken politics that has held the Rio Grande Valley back for decades — and Julio, a 26-year-old, fearless leader who was raised in this community and has spent his entire career fighting for the people who built it.
_They chose Julio._ And now the working people of the Rio Grande Valley will finally have a fighter representing them in Austin. That’s why the work we do in primary races is so important. With your grassroots support, we were able to ensure the Democratic nomination in a critical state like Texas was won by Julio, a true progressive voice, and not his establishment-pick opponent, who spent years voting with Republicans and attending Tea Party events.
And in TX-18, Christian Menefee is headed back to Congress to continue being a fearless fighter for his district. Christian has spent years taking on Trump and his allies in court — and winning. He’s been a powerful check on this administration's lawlessness, pushed back against their attacks on immigrant communities, and stood up to Greg Abbott’s corrupt political machine. Now he’s going back to Congress to keep fighting and delivering for the people of Houston.
**Julio & Christian mark our 10th and 11th wins this cycle — and I couldn’t be prouder of the impact we've been able to have in these races and across the country, because of your support.**
It’s wins like these that prove something I _know_ keeps the establishment up at night: you can’t fool voters by being a Democrat in name only. Earning voters' trust and winning elections means being a leader that does more than just talk. It means showing up for your community, getting in the ring to fight for them, and having the courage to take on the corporations and special interests that are making life harder for working people.
That’s Julio and Christian — exactly the kind of leaders this movement was built to back. We’re deeply proud to have endorsed them this cycle, and there’s so much more to come. More leaders to back, and more races to win. This momentum is real, and with your support, we’re going to keep fighting, keep building, and keep winning.
**[Will you pitch in $5 to help Leaders We Deserve continue backing leaders like Julio and Christian, and keep our winning streak going all the way to November?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260527_1_texas.GNtny5&refcode=em20260527-3528&amount=5&t=2&akid=3528%2E587540%2EgHoHED)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

subject: Let me be blunt about New Hampshire:

body:

Governor JB Pritzker here.
Let me be blunt: **_Everything we care about is on the line in 2026 — and New Hampshire could decide the outcome._**
We’ve already seen the damage Trump’s second term is inflicting on our country: His ICE agents are once again targeting families in broad daylight -- tearing apart communities, rounding up workers, and instilling fear across entire neighborhoods. He’s gutting environmental protections while utility rates spike, forcing working families to foot the bill so his billionaire donors can cash out.
He has no interest in bipartisanship, decency, or democracy. **And if Democrats don’t take back the Senate this November, there will be nothing stopping him.** That’s why we _must_ win in New Hampshire.
**[Chris Pappas is running in a tied race that could decide Senate control. Chip in $5 now to help him win.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260527_2.yrS3Ra&refcode=em20260527-2&t=2&akid=6864%2E582294%2E_-rsxy)**
Trump and his MAGA allies are laser-focused on New Hampshire. They’ve recruited a big-name candidate, they’re lining up GOP billionaire donors, and they know if they win here, they’ll shut the door on a Democratic Senate majority.
We can’t let that happen.
Chris Pappas is a fighter. He’s taken on Big Pharma, defended reproductive freedom, and delivered for working families in one of the toughest districts in the country.
I want him in the Senate. But we’re all going to have to come together to get him there. He’s running in a true battleground. His race is tied. And the GOP machine, desperate to keep Democrats locked out of power, is ready to bury him in dark money and attack ads.
**[That’s why I’m asking-- urgently -- for your help: Can you chip in $5 to help Chris Pappas win in New Hampshire and give us a fighting chance to stop Trump?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260527_2.yrS3Ra&refcode=em20260527-2&t=3&akid=6864%2E582294%2E_-rsxy)**

The damage is real. The stakes are massive. And the time to act is right now.
Thank you for standing with Chris and for standing up to the madness.

body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/PNG%202023%20TOP%20Newsletter%20Header.png]
Lea el boletín en español abajo [#Español]
Celebrating endorsed candidate wins in the Texas Dem. Primary Runoffs
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/2026%20endorsed%20runoff%20winners.jpg]
TOP PAC is proud to have played a part in lifting up progressive champions to big wins in Tuesday's primary runoffs.
We congratulate Congressman Christian Menefee (for TX-18), County Commissioner Dexter McCoy (for Fort Bend County Judge), Councilwoman Dr. Letitia Plummer (for Harris County Judge), and Adrian Reyna (for Texas HD 125) on their hard fought wins, and look forward to powering them to victory in the fall midterm.
From lowering costs for families, to fixing our failing healthcare system, to protecting our immigrant communities, Team Teal is ready to work alongside these community-powered candidates to deliver meaningful change for working Texans. Onward to November!
JUNE 11: Data Centers Movie and Discussion
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Data%20Center%20event.png]
Join TOP on Thursday, June 11 at the historic Texas Theatre in Dallas for a FREE documentary screening and discussion with community members to learn about data centers and how they can impact our communities.
From city to city across the country, these huge facilities are bringing with them higher water bills, increased pollution, and public health risks, while straining on our already unstable energy grid.
Reserve your FREE seat today, and bring a friend!
📆 Thursday, June 11th at 6 p.m.
📍Texas Theatre (231 Jefferson Blvd.)
🏆 Attendees have a chance to win a $100 gift card
For more information, contact Jet at (469) 550-4750.
https://secure.ngpvan.com/brQtPZN3UUCF83a4PjDSHw2 [https://secure.ngpvan.com/brQtPZN3UUCF83a4PjDSHw2]
THIS SATURDAY: Dallas Right2Justice Member Retreat
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Dallas%20staff%20and%20members.jpeg]
TOP's Right2Justice (R2J) campaign is continuing to sharpen around probation reform, non-safety traffic stops, and the broader criminalization pipeline — including the criminalizing of immigrant communities across the country.
Attend our next R2J member retreat this Saturday, May 30 in Dallas to learn more on latest campaign developments and how we can expand our efforts.
Contact Dr. Doshie Piper at dpiper@organizetexas.org [dpiper@organizetexas.org] for more retreat details and to reserve your spot.
TOP Tip: Sign the Willing to Fight Pledge
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Hear%20America.png]
If we want to stop harmful actions on our democracy and communities, we need millions of people fighting back together in peaceful and impactful ways. That's why TOP is proud to team up with our friends at the Organizing Revival Network to share their Willing to Fight Pledge, as we look to unite Texans on a vision that moves ALL communities forward.
👉🏾 TAKE ACTION NOW: Sign the pledge today! [https://www.willingtofight.org/orn]
https://secure.everyaction.com/_ew4evGgs0i4Ml7-RjD4tQ2 [https://secure.everyaction.com/_ew4evGgs0i4Ml7-RjD4tQ2]
Español
Celebrando las victorias de los candidatos respaldados en las segundas vueltas de las primarias demócratas de Texas
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/2026%20endorsed%20runoff%20winners.jpg]
TOP PAC se enorgullece de haber desempeñado un papel fundamental en impulsar a campeones progresistas hacia grandes victorias en las segundas vueltas de las elecciones primarias celebradas este martes.
Felicitamos al congresista Christian Menefee (por el distrito TX-18), al comisionado del condado Dexter McCoy (para Juez del Condado de Fort Bend), a la concejala Dra. Letitia Plummer (para Juez del Condado de Harris) y a Adrian Reyna (para el Distrito 125 de la Cámara de Representantes de Texas) por sus victorias, arduamente conquistadas; asimismo, esperamos con entusiasmo brindarles el impulso necesario para llevarlos a la victoria en las elecciones intermedias de otoño.
Desde la reducción de costos para las familias y la reparación de nuestro deficiente sistema de salud, hasta la protección de nuestras comunidades inmigrantes, el "Equipo Teal" está listo para trabajar codo con codo junto a estos candidatos —impulsados por la fuerza de la comunidad— con el fin de generar un cambio significativo para los trabajadores de Texas. ¡Adelante hacia noviembre!
11 de junio: Película y debate sobre centros de datos
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Data%20Center%20event.png]
Acompaña a TOP el jueves 11 de junio en el histórico Texas Theatre de Dallas para asistir a la proyección GRATUITA de un documental y participar en un debate con miembros de la comunidad, con el fin de aprender sobre los centros de datos y cómo estos pueden afectar a nuestras comunidades.
De ciudad en ciudad, a lo largo y ancho del país, estas enormes instalaciones traen consigo facturas de agua más elevadas, un aumento de la contaminación y riesgos para la salud pública, al tiempo que ejercen una presión adicional sobre nuestra ya inestable red energética.
¡Reserva hoy mismo su asiento GRATUITO y trae a un amigo!
📆 Jueves 11 de junio a las 6:00 p.m.
📍 Texas Theatre (231 Jefferson Blvd.)
🏆 Los asistentes tendrán la oportunidad de ganar una tarjeta de regalo de $100
Para más información, comuníquese con Jet al (469) 550-4750.
https://secure.ngpvan.com/brQtPZN3UUCF83a4PjDSHw2 [https://secure.ngpvan.com/brQtPZN3UUCF83a4PjDSHw2]
ESTE SÁBADO: Reunión de miembros de Dallas Right2Justice
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Dallas%20staff%20and%20members.jpeg]
La campaña Right2Justice (R2J) de TOP continúa enfocándose cada vez más en la reforma del régimen de libertad condicional, las detenciones de tráfico no relacionadas con la seguridad y el proceso más amplio de criminalización —incluida la criminalización de las comunidades inmigrantes en todo el país.
Asista a nuestro próximo reunión de miembros de R2J el sábado 30 de mayo en Dallas para conocer los últimos avances de la campaña y descubrir cómo podemos ampliar nuestros esfuerzos.
Comuníquese con la Dra. Doshie Piper en dpiper@organizetexas.org [dpiper@organizetexas.org] para obtener más detalles sobre la reunión y reservar su lugar.
Consejos de TOP: Firma el Compromiso de Luchar
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Hear%20America.png]
Si queremos detener las acciones perjudiciales contra nuestra democracia y nuestras comunidades, necesitamos a millones de personas luchando juntas de manera pacífica y contundente. Por eso, en TOP nos enorgullece unir fuerzas con nuestros amigos de Organizing Revival para difundir su «Compromiso de Lucha» (Willing to Fight Pledge), con el objetivo de unir a los tejanos en torno a una visión que impulse el progreso de TODAS las comunidades.

[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._nQ/s0s597d2cd1)
It has been just over five years. No one has been held accountable.
That is how Erin Lee describes what happened on May 4, 2021 and everything since. Federal litigation, Supreme Court petitions and public records battles have produced thousands of pages of emails, court filings and internal policies. “It’s been an insane five years,” she told RMV in May.
The Lees moved from Florida to Wellington, Colorado in 2020. Erin says she and her husband were “faithless, left-leaning parents” with a close relationship with their daughter. In spring 2021 that daughter had just turned twelve and was enrolled at Wellington Middle School. Her homeroom and art teacher was Jenna Riep, also the school’s Gender and Sexualities Alliance (GSA) sponsor.

**[Colorado’s annual seat belt crackdown returns. The numbers suggest it isn’t working.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._nQ/s2q2c2c36d5)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice._nQ/s5r620faf8e)
* **Five years of data, zero progress:** Colorado's annual Click It or Ticket campaign launched again this week, but CDOT's own numbers show the unbuckled share of passenger vehicle deaths has held steady between 48% and 52% every year since 2021 — with 191 Coloradans dying unbelted last year alone, representing 50.4% of all passenger vehicle fatalities.
* **The law itself is the problem:** Colorado remains a secondary enforcement state, meaning officers cannot stop a driver solely for not wearing a seat belt — a separate violation must occur first — and the fine when they are caught is just $65, which NHTSA's own guidance acknowledges may be too low to change behavior.
* **Two fixes exist, neither has passed:** Research consistently points to two effective policy levers — primary enforcement for all adult occupants and higher fines — neither of which is current Colorado law, and neither of which advanced this legislative session, leaving the same demographic most at risk: young men, pickup truck drivers, and nighttime rural road travelers.

subject: A reminder about Women’s Rights
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Emerge America
body:
https://emergeamerica.org/ [https://emergeamerica.org/]
Dear Peter ,
The recent case of a woman giving birth inside a Brooklyn courtroom during her arraignment has sparked national attention and renewed concerns about how pregnant women are treated within the justice system.
Samantha Randazzo, 33, went into labor while waiting to appear before a judge on low-level charges, ultimately delivering her baby in the courtroom late Friday night. It is alleged that Randazzo gave birth while restrained and without adequate medical care or privacy. Court officials dispute portions of those claims, and investigations and calls for accountability are ongoing.
What remains clear, however, is that women continue to need strong advocacy — especially in moments where dignity, safety, and basic care are at stake.
Women still remain underrepresented across many systems of power and leadership, with women making up only about 13% of sworn police officers and roughly one-third of the judiciary — numbers that still fall far short of parity.
That is why organizations like Emerge play such an important role. From Gavel In [https://emergeamerica.org/candidate-training/judicial-program/] , our award-winning judicial training program, to our Signature program [https://emergeamerica.org/candidate-training/signature-program/] , we create opportunities and pathways for women to get elected to and serve in positions where laws are written, systems are overseen, and decisions are made.
Increasing women’s leadership is essential to building institutions that are more equitable, compassionate, and responsive to the people they serve – so start training today. [https://emergeamerica.org/candidate-training/]
-Jill Barkley Roy
Director, Emerge Action Fund

Now we have 6 days left to finish the job.

The political establishment and billionaire-backed Super PACs are absolutely going to spend heavily to stop this movement from winning. They know what’s at stake here.

They know this race is about more than one congressional seat.

It’s about whether a new generation of leadership can actually break through.

So we’re asking if you can help us push through the final 6 days of this race.

subject: Nancy Mace
body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20260527-2304-foote&t=1001&akid=2304%2E342411%2EgaeguI ]Squad Victory Fund

Nancy Mace is coming after me... again.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/20304?c0=svfem-20260527-movement._0Xv9Y&refcode=em20260527-2304&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=2304%2E342411%2EgaeguI ]Tweet from @RepNancyMace: 'Ilhan Omar. Shri Thanedar. Pramila Jayapal.
All born in foreign countries, none were citizens by birth. All sitting in
United States Congress. All making clear every single day their loyalty is
not to America. We just introduced a long overdue joint resolution
proposing a constitutional amendment to require Members of Congress,
federal judges, and Senate-confirmed officers to be natural born citizens.
This is the very same standard the President and Vice President are
already required to meet. The people writing America's laws, confirming
America's judges, and representing America on the world stage should have
one loyalty: America. Not any other country. For too long we have allowed
foreign born members to hold seats in this government while making clear
they are America last, not America first. We see it every day. This
constitutional amendment will put an end to it.

Peter, Nancy Mace
wants us to be silent. She wants us to be afraid. She wants an America for
her, and only for people who look like her. But that’s not what this
country is, and it never has been.

I’m a refugee, and I was given the opportunity for a new start in America.
I am eternally grateful for everything this country has given me. I ran
for Congress in the first place because I believe in America’s promise,
and I am never going to stop working to make sure we live up to that
promise.

I can stand against anything people like Nancy Mace and Donald Trump throw
my way because I have lived through things far worse than they can ever

name: Dr. Shirley Weber
subject: Respectfully asking for your vote
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Shirley Weber for Secretary of State 2026
body:
https://drshirleyweber.com/?utm_source=email%20wrapper&utm_medium=email%20wrapper&utm_campaign=email%20wrapper [https://drshirleyweber.com/?utm_source=email%20wrapper&utm_medium=email%20wrapper&utm_campaign=email%20wrapper]
Dear friends,

I’m writing today to respectfully ask for your vote in the June primary.

I was born in the Jim Crow South to sharecroppers who were denied the right to vote. California gave our family a new beginning — my parents cast their first ballots here and even opened our living room as a polling place for our neighbors. That is the California I have dedicated my life to protecting.

America is the only country in the world where, within a single generation, a family can go from disenfranchisement under Jim Crow to administering elections in the largest state in the nation. I have lived that journey firsthand. And I refuse to let anyone roll it back.

We are not in normal times. There are forces working right now to shorten polling hours, reduce early voting days, eliminate vote-by-mail, and intimidate the election workers who make democracy run. Some have even threatened the lives of those officials when their preferred candidate loses. That behavior has no place in California, and as long as I am Secretary of State, it will not be tolerated.

During my tenure, 28 statewide and special elections were successfully administered. When our voting rights came under attack, I took the fight to the courts and won. I have always led with transparency because I believe trust is the foundation of everything we do.

Every eligible Californian deserves a clear, unobstructed path to the ballot box, regardless of party, regardless of politics. That has always been my commitment to you, and it always will be.

Ballots must be postmarked by June 2 in order to be counted. If you have not already, please make a plan to return your ballot [vote.ca.gov] – and I hope that you’ll consider casting a vote for me to continue serving as California’s Secretary of State. Make a plan » [vote.ca.gov] Your ballot is your voice. It is a precious gift — the ability to weigh in on the pressing issues of the day, to protect our rights, to build a more equitable society. Too many people throughout history, including members of my own family, never got that chance. So please don't let it go to waste.

Together, let’s keep fighting to ensure that every Californian has the opportunity to participate in safe, transparent, and accessible elections.

Gratefully,

-Dr. Shirley N. Weber

clean_body: [] Dear friends, I’m writing today to respectfully ask for your vote in the June primary. I was born in the Jim Crow South to sharecroppers who were denied the right to vote. California gave our family a new beginning — my parents cast their first ballots here and even opened our living room as a polling place for our neighbors. That is the California I have dedicated my life to protecting. America is the only country in the world where, within a single generation, a family can go from disenfranchisement under Jim Crow to administering elections in the largest state in the nation. I have lived that journey firsthand. And I refuse to let anyone roll it back. We are not in normal times. There are forces working right now to shorten polling hours, reduce early voting days, eliminate vote-by-mail, and intimidate the election workers who make democracy run. Some have even threatened the lives of those officials when their preferred candidate loses. That behavior has no place in California, and as long as I am Secretary of State, it will not be tolerated. During my tenure, 28 statewide and special elections were successfully administered. When our voting rights came under attack, I took the fight to the courts and won. I have always led with transparency because I believe trust is the foundation of everything we do. Every eligible Californian deserves a clear, unobstructed path to the ballot box, regardless of party, regardless of politics. That has always been my commitment to you, and it always will be. Ballots must be postmarked by June 2 in order to be counted. If you have not already, please make a plan to return your ballot [vote.ca.gov] – and I hope that you’ll consider casting a vote for me to continue serving as California’s Secretary of State. Make a plan » [vote.ca.gov] Your ballot is your voice. It is a precious gift — the ability to weigh in on the pressing issues of the day, to protect our rights, to build a more equitable society. Too many people throughout history, including members of my own family, never got that chance. So please don't let it go to waste. Together, let’s keep fighting to ensure that every Californian has the opportunity to participate in safe, transparent, and accessible elections. Gratefully, -Dr. Shirley N. body:
Peter, the radical Left is letting the floodgates fly open.

They want to dilute **YOUR** legal vote with a system that lets anyone walk off the street and into a voting booth.

Friends,
For nearly 25 years, I represented our nation around the world. During my time as USCIS’s Director of International Operations, I helped coordinate responses to a wide variety of national emergencies, and I’m proud of my time spent working to keep Americans safe. I’ll take the same commitment to service to Congress, but I need your help to get there.
We need to raise $10,000 by the end of the month to keep our organizing efforts on track — can you please donate any amount today?
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/trina-swanson-may-email?&amount=25&refcode=20260527]
One of the most important things I learned during my time in this public service is how fragile democracies can become. All it takes is one determined authoritarian leader willing to tear down the pillars of representative government, and unfortunately what we’re seeing here at home reminds me of the type of democratic erosion I’ve seen in other nations.
The MAGA movement has consolidated power in the hands of a president who is determined to tilt the scales of our democracy in his favor. Trump has coordinated with the Supreme Court to allow Republican states to disenfranchise voters for political gain, and he’s threatened to use federal law enforcement officers to disrupt elections across the nation. Even though polls show that Trump’s approval rating continues to fall, Democrats face a tough battle to retake the House due to Republican gerrymandering and voter suppression efforts.
Winning in districts like ours is critical to flipping the House blue and delivering results for central and northern Minnesota. My roots have always been here in Minnesota — I understand what our communities need, and how to get results. That’s why I won the DFL nomination and our people-powered campaign is getting ready to compete in every corner of this huge district.

body:
A letter from me why that matters. | [](http://links.burtjonesforga.com/u/click?_t=858b83d5086141569cc77db3b7b1b605&_m=21adc1f39dcd430390908f305e494e31&_e=yFWkSaWmYi-GOS7knLwIG8cg-B2kx2p5277pGYYp5FB_BPTHW0C0N88D6RuJ2shySNkq5xbNGtzsUVaU67CYrU4HDizztH3WmtP_corQsOgtizFbIs7BwQ-ecg6QNvwf5UYEd4r7rC2gxt5cgVVpdV4g6cledUrZW7vdacPrH-5B7HhPFNIaz_VKI82DmCQpyPRNPUbSk1eqfF7jUprwjUueYoK29bZuKQx7t04QuNRuhWoDC5kp7cNsl_A8sm5vKVm51WTe5RHtSw4e_yaBhykICs8s7FD7dyxgcQQNy6QUf3RWc4MAQ4eUzREaNKfS)

---

Peter,

I need to be straight with you about what's happening in this race.

Rick Jackson won't debate me before you vote. The Atlanta Press Club debate is this Monday, June 1st and he's still dodging it.

Here's how it went down: I offered June 1st. He said June 14th - **after** early voting ends. Atlanta News First tried to split the difference with June 7th or 8th. Slick Rick Jackson held firm on the 14th.

You deserve to hear from both of us before you cast your ballot. Side by side. Answering tough questions. Defending our records. That's how this is supposed to work.

But they're hiding Jackson the way Democrats hid Biden - and we know why. A guy who donated to Stacey Abrams and Liz Cheney, employed illegal immigrants at his mansion, and ran a Medicare kickback scheme? He's got plenty to answer for. And apparently, plenty to hide.

I'll be at that debate. The podium next to me should have Rick Jackson behind it. Instead, Georgia voters might be staring at an empty stage.

**That's not right.**

If you agree that voters deserve to hear from BOTH candidates before the first ballot is cast, make some noise. Share this email. Post on social media and Rick’s posts. Let them know dodging debates isn't what Georgia leaders do.

I'm ready to debate. Ready to answer your questions. Ready to earn your vote.

_Will Rick Jackson show up?_

See you June 1st,

**Burt Jones**
Lieutenant Governor of Georgia

And now, it’s helping Mark fight back against his most serious challenge yet — taking on the full weight of the Executive Branch. But here’s something we thought you should know: Out of the millions of people who support Mark, less than 25% of them have made a donation to support his work. Today, we’re asking you to join that important group. Mark’s average online donation is around $27. Most people chip in much less than that. But with so much at stake this November, all that matters is that you’re helping us support critical races across the country. We’ll put it to work right away as Mark campaigns to elect Democrats up and down the ballot to hold Donald Trump and this Administration accountable. Trump's judicial nominees
are being handed the easiest possible test: Who won the 2020 election? Was
January 6th an attack on the U.S. Capitol?

They won't answer. They dodge, deflect, and hide behind canned non-answers
— signaling loyalty to Trump over the law and over the people whose rights
they'd be sworn to protect.

And nineteen Senate Democrats continue to vote to move them forward
anyway.

Yes...nineteen. Let that sink in.

These are the same senators who call themselves a check on this
administration. Who swear they're fighting Trump's abuses of power. But
when it counts, they look at nominees who won't acknowledge basic reality
— and wave them through.

It's hypocrisy. It's complicity. And the American people deserve to know.

Every one of these confirmations is permanent. These judges will be on the
bench long after Trump is gone — ruling on your voting rights, your civil
rights, your healthcare. There are no do-overs.

Enough is enough. We’re calling out these crooked nominees, Trump’s
court-packing scheme, and the Democrats enabling them. Letting this slide
is exactly how democracy erodes — confirmation by confirmation.
